# Statistical support (generated by scripts/significance.py -- do not edit)

## 1. SCA seed statistics vs single-run baselines (two-stage T->V R@1)

| benchmark | SCA mean +- sd (n=3) | 95% CI | GRAM* | PMRL* | HyperGRAM+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MSR-VTT | 54.6 +- 0.2 | [54.1, 55.2] | 52.5 (outside CI) | 54.3 (inside CI) | 54.0 (outside CI) |
| DiDeMo | 51.2 +- 0.3 | [50.6, 51.9] | 50.7 (inside CI) | 52.5 (outside CI) | 48.9 (outside CI) |
| ActivityNet | 55.9 +- 0.2 | [55.6, 56.3] | 56.3 (inside CI) | 54.1 (outside CI) | 53.7 (outside CI) |
| VATEX | 90.6 +- 0.1 | [90.3, 90.9] | 90.0 (outside CI) | 89.6 (outside CI) | 89.8 (outside CI) |
| AudioCaps | 35.0 +- 0.4 | [34.0, 36.0] | 32.2 (outside CI) | 34.4 (inside CI) | -- |

Baselines are released checkpoints: n=1 by nature, so no two-sample test exists. "outside CI" says the observed ordering is not explained by SCA seed variance; it says nothing about the baseline's own variance.

## 2. Exact sign tests

- Masked-aggregator (Table 3): SCA beats GRAM in 25/25 cells; exact one-sided sign test p = 2.98e-08. Cells within a benchmark share nested masks, so conservatively treating each BENCHMARK as one unit: 5/5, p = 0.0312.
- Aggregation gain: 12/14 baseline method x benchmark cells negative; against a fusion-helps-or-hurts-equally null, exact one-sided p = 0.0065. (Method rows share checkpoints across benchmarks -- the cells are not fully independent; the count itself is the primary evidence.)

## 3. Measured eval noise floor

Repeat evaluations of identical checkpoints (harvest, 15 cells): max ITM R@1 spread 0.2. Margins at or below this are not results; every headline margin in the paper is quoted against it.
